meta.purpose: Reference unit sizes by bedroom count, used by the deal calculator to ESTIMATE gross building area from a unit mix on request. Nothing here auto-fills: the user picks a reference standard, sees the working, and clicks to apply. Every figure below is from a jurisdiction other than Colorado and is labelled as such on screen.

colorado.note: Colorado CHFA's Housing Tax Credit Qualified Allocation Plan sets no minimum unit size by bedroom count. Unit sizes appear in the QAP only as applicant-supplied fields (unit mix and size worksheet, market study review). Verified by full-text search of the 2025-2026 QAP and the 2027-2028 QAP third draft for 'square feet', 'unit size' and 'minimum'.

sources.title: CHFA Housing Tax Credit Qualified Allocation Plan 2025-2026
CHFA Housing Tax Credit Qualified Allocation Plan 2027-2028, third draft

efficiency.label: Building efficiency: net rentable area divided by gross building area
efficiency.note: Trade-press benchmarks, not a regulatory figure. Meeks (2005) reports conventional apartments averaging 70 to 75 percent net-to-gross with 82 percent or higher achievable through efficient layouts; Hildahl (2022) illustrates 85 percent. The default of 0.80 sits inside that range and is shown on screen so it can be changed.

sources.title: Donald Meeks, AIA, 'Cost Cutters', Multifamily Executive, 2005-06-03
sources.quote: apartments have been far less efficient, with an average ratio of 70 percent to 75 percent

sources.title: Blair Hildahl, 'Apartment Developers: Higher Efficiency = Higher ROI', BASE4, 2022-06-08
sources.quote: 100,000 square feet of gross area has 85,000 square feet of actual rentable space

meta.fruita_fixture_note: The repo's worked example (data/fixtures/fruita-commons-*.scenario.json) carries modeled unit ranges averaging about 1,135 net SF per unit. The old gross-area placeholder of 62,000 SF for 60 units (about 1,033 gross SF per unit) described a smaller program than that example and was removed; the field now stays blank until entered or estimated.

standards.label: NC Housing Finance Agency 2026 QAP Appendix B design minimums
standards.measure: Heated square feet, measured interior wall to interior wall, excluding exterior walls and unheated areas
standards.source_note: Appendix B, 2026 Design Quality Standards and Requirements, section C.1 'All residential units must meet minimum unit size requirements'. Studio 375, 1 Bedroom 660, 2 Bedroom 900, 3 Bedroom 1,100, 4 Bedroom 1,250 square feet.

standards.label: Washington RCW 36.70A.819 affordable unit size (largest size a city may require)
standards.measure: Square feet; the statute caps what cities and counties may require of affordable units, so these are floors of what an affordable unit must be allowed to be, not design minimums
standards.source_note: 2025 c 139 s 9: '400 square feet for a studio unit; 550 square feet for a one-bedroom unit; 750 square feet for a two-bedroom unit; and 1,000 square feet for a three-bedroom unit.' No four-bedroom figure, so a mix with 4BR units cannot be estimated under this reference.
